worked_solution:
Euler's method approximates the solution of an initial value problem containing a system of ODEs by applying the update rule component-wise to each equation.

Since we want to find the values of $y,$ $z,$ and $w$ at $x=1,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=1-\frac{1}{4}=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

First, we place the initial condition data in a table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |  |  | $1$ |  |  | $-2$ |  |  |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′},$ ${z}^{′},$ and ${w}^{′}$ according to the given rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =2y-z+x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}-1+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4} \\ {z}^{′} & =z+w \\  & =1+(-2) \\  & =-1 \\ {w}^{′} & =\frac{xz}{2y} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{4})\cdot 1}{2\cdot \frac{1}{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add these to our table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |  | $1$ | $-1$ |  | $-2$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |  |

Next, we compute $Δy,$ $Δz,$ and $Δw$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{3}{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{16} \\ Δz & ={z}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(-1)\cdot \frac{3}{4} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4} \\ Δw & ={w}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{3}{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

We add these to our table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{3}{16}$ | $1$ | $-1$ | $-\frac{3}{4}$ | $-2$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{3}{16}$ |

To get the new values of $x,$ $y,$ $z,$ and $w$ in the *next* row, we add $Δx$ to $x,$ $Δy$ to $y,$ $Δz$ to $z,$ and $Δw$ to $w,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=\frac{1}{4}+\frac{3}{4}=1 \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{16}=\frac{11}{16} \\ {z}_{\text{new}} & =z+Δz=1+(-\frac{3}{4})=\frac{1}{4} \\ {w}_{\text{new}} & =w+Δw=-2+\frac{3}{16}=-\frac{29}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these values to our table in a new row gives the following:

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{3}{16}$ | $1$ | $-1$ | $-\frac{3}{4}$ | $-2$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{3}{16}$ |
| $1$ | $\frac{11}{16}$ |  |  | $\frac{1}{4}$ |  |  | $-\frac{29}{16}$ |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
y(1)≈\frac{11}{16},\,z(1)≈\frac{1}{4},\,w(1)≈-\frac{29}{16}.
$$
html:
Euler's method approximates the solution of an initial value problem containing a system of ODEs by applying the update rule component-wise to each equation.

Since we want to find the values of y, z, and w at x=1, we will use a step size of Δx=1−14=34.

First, we place the initial condition data in a table.

x y y′ Δy z z′ Δz w w′ Δw
14 12 1 −2

Next, we compute y′, z′, and w′ according to the given rules: y′=2y−z+x=2⋅12−1+14=14z′=z+w=1+(−2)=−1w′=xz2y=(14)⋅12⋅12=14

So, we add these to our table.

x y y′ Δy z z′ Δz w w′ Δw
14 12 14 1 −1 −2 14

Next, we compute Δy, Δz, and Δw using Euler's method: Δy=y′⋅Δx=14⋅34=316Δz=z′⋅Δx=(−1)⋅34=−34Δw=w′⋅Δx=14⋅34=316

We add these to our table.

x y y′ Δy z z′ Δz w w′ Δw
14 12 14 316 1 −1 −34 −2 14 316

To get the new values of x, y, z, and w in the next row, we add Δx to x, Δy to y, Δz to z, and Δw to w, as follows: xnew=x+Δx=14+34=1ynew=y+Δy=12+316=1116znew=z+Δz=1+(−34)=14wnew=w+Δw=−2+316=−2916

Adding these values to our table in a new row gives the following:

x y y′ Δy z z′ Δz w w′ Δw
14 12 14 316 1 −1 −34 −2 14 316
1 1116 14 −2916

Therefore, we conclude that y(1)≈1116,z(1)≈14,w(1)≈−2916.
